summary.text: Diana Harshbarger is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 1st District, a licensed pharmacist and business owner from Kingsport who first took office in January 2021 after winning the open seat. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where she is vice chair of the Health Subcommittee, and is seeking re-election in November 2026.

paragraphs.text: Born in Bloomingdale, Tennessee, a community outside Kingsport; according to her official biography, she was the first in her immediate family to graduate from high school and college.
Attended East Tennessee State University and earned a Doctor of Pharmacy degree from Mercer University College of Pharmacy.
Returned to the Kingsport area after graduation to start a business, and has been a licensed pharmacist and business owner for over three decades, according to her official biography.
Served as a board member of the International Academy of Compounding Pharmacists.
Won the August 6, 2020 Republican primary and the November 2020 general election for the open 1st District seat, succeeding Rep. Phil Roe, and took office January 3, 2021.
In the 117th Congress (2021-2022) she was assigned to the Homeland Security and Education and the Workforce committees; since 2023 she has served on Energy and Commerce.

In the 119th Congress she serves on Energy and Commerce as vice chair of the Subcommittee on Health and as a member of the Subcommittees on Oversight and Investigations and on Energy, and co-chairs the Congressional Bipartisan Rural Health Caucus and several other caucuses.

Her official biography says she teaches Sunday school, helps with her church's mission work, belongs to the local Chamber of Commerce, and lives in Kingsport and on a farm in Unicoi with her husband, Robert; she has one son and two grandsons.
